title: Your first image: write a Dockerfile, build it, run it
skills: Dockerfile FROM / WORKDIR / COPY / RUN / CMD
docker build -t and the layer cache

ticket.subject: sensor-api: ship it as an image
body: The dashboards team wants to run `sensor-api` (the FastAPI app in `app/`) without installing Python. Please
write its `Dockerfile` and try it on your machine:
- **Base image** `python:3.12-slim`: a pinned, small Python. Never `latest`, which changes under your feet.
- **Fast rebuilds**: we change `app/main.py` many times a day. A change there must not reinstall the
dependencies: the `pip install` layer has to come from the cache.
- **The command** starts `uvicorn app.main:app` on port 8000, in the JSON (exec) form, reachable from outside
- Build it as `sensor-api:0.1`, run it in the background as a container named `sensor-api` with the app's
port 8000 published on port **8080** of your machine, check it with `docker ps`, and call
This is the lab's simulated Docker engine: nothing is built, pulled or run, and your files are read, never

hints: A Dockerfile is read top to bottom: `FROM` the base image, `WORKDIR /app`, `COPY` files in, `RUN` a command at build time, `CMD` the command the container starts with.

Each instruction is a layer, cached until it or what it copies changes, and every layer after a changed one is rebuilt. `COPY requirements.txt .` then `RUN pip install ...` then `COPY app ./app` keeps the install cached when only the code changes.

`CMD ["uvicorn", "app.main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000"]`: uvicorn listens on 127.0.0.1 by default, which inside a container is the container itself, so a published port could never reach it.
`docker run -d --name sensor-api -p 8080:8000 sensor-api:0.1`: `-p HOST:CONTAINER`. `docker ps` lists running containers, `docker logs sensor-api` shows what the app printed.

The lint findings at the end of `docker build` explain what to improve (DL3007: unpinned base, DL3025: shell-form command, DP001: code copied before the dependencies). `docker history sensor-api:0.1` lists the layers.
Changed the Dockerfile? Build again: a container keeps the image it started from, so remove it (`docker rm -f sensor-api`) and run it again from the new image.
